Article Title: A Florida mother earned $1,500 a month while her new husband paid $8,600 in household bills, but a judge counted both as her income in a child-support dispute; on October 21, an appeals court ordered
Article Text:
Florida court ordered fresh child-support calculation after husband's household payments were counted as wife's income. (AI image)

Parents' financial arrangement changed

Why mother's income was calculated at $10,100

Appeals court disagreed with the lower court

What happens to the child-support payments now?

A Florida appeals court on Wednesday ordered a fresh calculation of child support in a dispute involving a mother whose monthly income of $1,500 had been assessed at $10,100 after a lower court included $8,600 paid by her new husband towards household expenses.According to the judgment document available on Justia, Bianca Rampartap had sought higher child support from her former husband, Darryl Rampartap, who had moved to Trinidad and stopped spending parenting time with their child. After the lower court included the money spent by her new husband as her income, the appeals court has now ruled that it could not be treated as her income simply because he covered those expenses.Rampartap and her former husband, Darryl Rampartap, divorced in 2016. Nearly a decade later, their disagreement over financial support for their child brought them back to court. By then, Bianca had remarried, while Darryl had moved abroad.The dispute arose after Bianca sought a change in child support because she was caring for their child without any parenting time being exercised by Darryl. Although the court accepted that their circumstances had changed, the calculation of the revised payment created another problem.The court assessed Bianca's new husband's expenses as part of her finances, even though her own reported earnings were much lower. In her challenge to the decision, Bianca maintained that money spent by her husband on their shared household was not income paid to her.When Bianca and Darryl divorced in 2016, they were given equal parenting time. They also had to share the costs of their child's extracurricular activities, uniforms, equipment and summer camp. Bianca was responsible for 40% of those expenses, while Darryl had to cover the remaining 60%.No child-support payment was ordered initially. In 2018, however, the court directed Darryl to pay $225.42 in child support, described in the judgment as bimonthly. The parents were also asked to divide the costs of extracurricular activities and summer camp equally.The arrangement continued until Bianca approached the court again in 2024. She said Darryl had left the United States and was no longer spending overnight time with their child, despite the earlier arrangement being based on shared parenting.The court found that Darryl had not exercised his parenting time for eight months. It also accepted testimony that he was permanently living in Trinidad. Bianca was then given full parenting time, sole parental responsibility and authority to make decisions concerning their child.The earlier child-support arrangement thus needed to be reviewed. The court therfore referred the financial question to a hearing officer, who examined the parents' incomes and expenses before recommending a new payment.Bianca told the hearing officer that she earned $1,500 a month before deductions. Her financial statement also showed that her current husband was covering household expenses of $8,600 every month.The hearing officer added those expenses to Bianca's earnings, arriving at a monthly income of $10,100. The reasoning was that her husband's payments reduced the amount she needed to spend on maintaining the household.This figure was then used to calculate the parents' respective contributions. Darryl was ordered to pay $403 a month in child support from July 2025. He also owed $1,953.38 in payments dating back to August 2024.Bianca objected to the calculation, arguing that her husband's financial contribution to their home should not be treated in the same way as money she personally earned or received. After the lower court rejected her attempts to challenge the decision, she appealed.The appeals court focused on the difference between receiving financial help and sharing household expenses with a spouse.Florida law allows certain payments made on someone's behalf to be included when calculating their income. However, the judges found that Bianca's husband was paying expenses for the home in which he also lived. The payments were not made to Bianca, and there was no sufficient evidence to justify adding the entire $8,600 to her income.The judgment read, “When the new husband merely paid the household expenses for his own household, no ‘payment,’ in kind or otherwise, had been made to his wife.”The court explained that financial assistance from relatives or other people could still qualify as income in some situations. What mattered was whether the money was actually being provided to the parent, rather than simply being spent on a shared home.The appeals court also noticed an inconsistency in the earlier financial figures. Bianca's income had been recorded as $10,100 before deductions and $10,487 after deductions. The judges believed the two figures had been mistakenly switched.Using those figures, the earlier calculation had assigned Bianca 80.43% of the parents' combined income and Darryl 19.57%. Those percentages helped determine the amount Darryl was required to pay.The appeals court has now directed the lower court to determine Bianca's income again and recalculate the child-support obligations.
Article Summary: Florida court ordered fresh child-support calculation after husband's household payments were counted as wife's income. Parents' financial arrangement changed after parents divorced in 2016. Court assessed Bianca's new husband's expenses as part of her finances, even though her own reported earnings were much lower.

Article Title: Dutch scientists built a tiny robotic arm using living algae and two layers of gel; controlled by light, the two-centimetre strip grasped a metal ball and lifted a rubber ring underwater without a con
Article Text:
Researchers use light to trigger living algae’s metabolism, enabling the tiny robotic arm to bend without electrical signals.

Living cell robot

The control system is lightweight

From bending to taking

Building robots using biology

Think of a robot without battery, without traditional motor and without complicated mechanical joints and only living microalgae, soft gels and source of light. That’s the unusual premise of a new experiment by researchers at Delft University of Technology in the Netherlands, who have constructed a miniature actuator that can bend, grasp and lift objects underwater. The work offers a glimpse of such a future, where living organisms could become an active part of the robotic systems. Scroll down for more.Phys Org reports that the soft robotic strip is tiny, about two centimeters long and one millimeter thick, but its movement is surprisingly sophisticated. The actuator consists of two layers of hydrogel that respond differently when the chemical environment changes and microalgae grow over the surface of the actuator, the research report says.The report, published by Nature Communications, states the device utilizes the biological activity of the algae to generate movement rather than a traditional motor. They photosynthesize in the presence of light, converting light and carbon dioxide into energy. They also use nitrogen to grow their cells. This activity changes the chemical environment inside the hydrogel. The result is a change of pH which causes different degrees of swelling of the two gel layers.That imbalance makes the strip bend and curve.By simply changing the lighting conditions, the researchers can control the movement, the study report from Phys Org and Nature Communications says. When the light is turned off, the biological processes inside the algae change the pH in the opposite direction and the actuator starts bending back.This is quite a quick response, the strip beginning to move back in the opposite direction in about 10 seconds. This gives the little device a kind of biological control system. Instead of sending electrical signals to a motor, researchers can use light to induce a physical response generated through the metabolism of living organisms.The researchers wanted to see if this movement could do more than just demonstrate an unusual biological response, according to Nature Communications. For the underwater experiments the actuator was designed for simple manipulation tasks, such as hooking and lifting a rubber ring and grasping a small metal ball.Such motions could eventually be useful in situations where gentle handling is important. Soft robotic structures could more flexibly interact with fragile objects and changing environment than rigid mechanical systems.The technology could also result in devices that imitate movements found in nature. Light responsive mechanisms could someday be used for things like blinds that can change their orientation automatically or agricultural systems that can change their position based on environmental conditions.The experiment's importance is beyond its tiny scale. The researchers are investigating a wider region where living cells are incorporated directly into functional materials, enabling biological processes to yield useful mechanical behavior.Microalgae are of particular interest since they can use light as an energy source by photosynthesis. This opens the way to soft robotic systems that need less conventional external energy, but practical applications are a longer-term prospect.The research, published in Nature Communications, is an early proof of concept, not a ready-to-use robotic technology. But it points to an interesting direction in engineering: machines that don’t just copy biology, but actually collaborate with living things to move.Inside this tiny underwater arm, light does more than illuminate; it is the signal that converts biological activity into motion.Images Courtesy: istock
Article Summary: Researchers at Delft University of Technology in the Netherlands have constructed a miniature actuator that can bend, grasp and lift objects underwater. They used light to trigger living algae’s metabolism, enabling the tiny robotic arm to bend without electrical signals. The work offers a glimpse of such a future, where living organisms could become an active part of the robotic systems.

Article Title: A 10-foot endangered shark trapped in a South Korean canal for more than a month was finally guided toward the open sea; hours after its third rescue attempt, it swam back, leaving officials searching
Article Text:
Bukangi has been in the North Port canal since September 18 (Reuters photo)

Why three attempts to move Bukangi have failed

Busy port could be influencing the shark

Shark's prolonged stay is concerning

A 10-foot endangered shark in South Korea has left authorities facing an unusual rescue problem. After spending more than a month inside a canal in the port city of Busan, the shark was finally guided towards the open sea on Wednesday. But the rescue lasted only a few hours as the animal swam underneath a barrier net and returned to the canal, forcing officials to reconsider their approach after three attempts to move it out.The female dusky shark, known locally as Bukangi, has been in the North Port canal since September 18, according to news agency Associated Press. Its presence has turned the waterfront into a popular attraction, with more than 1.7 million people visiting the area. Busan authorities have also adopted the shark as a city mascot.Officials worry about how long Bukangi can remain in the confined waterway as they have found no clear signs that it has been feeding regularly during its stay. Water temperatures are also beginning to fall, raising fears about the possible effects on its health.According to Reuters, officials have placed barriers to prevent it from travelling farther inside.The outer net has also been opened in the hope that it will move towards the sea voluntarily. Meanwhile, experts have advised against another immediate rescue attempt as Bukangi's condition remains stable.After two failed attempts to get the shark out of the canal, rescuers tried a new approach. Instead of relying mainly on boats and nets to block the shark's movements, workers used floating platforms to gradually direct it towards the canal entrance. Divers also participated in the effort.On Wednesday, the plan appeared to work. Bukangi moved beyond the canal and spent several hours in nearby waters. But by night, it had found a route beneath the outer net and returned.When it subsequently became confined between two barriers near the entrance, officials strengthened the nets farther inside the canal while leaving a route towards open water.During operations carried out on September 29 and October 2, workers used boats spraying streams of water and nets across the waterway. However, Bukangi avoided the boats and managed to pass over the nets.The reason Bukangi has remained in the canal is still unknown. Scientists have also been examining whether conditions outside the waterway could explain its reluctance to leave.Busan's North Port handles container ships and cruise vessels, making it a busy maritime area. Kim Hyun-woo, a senior researcher at South Korea's National Institute of Fisheries Science, believes the activity around the port could be influencing the shark's behaviour.According to Kim, the relatively quiet canal may appear safer than the surrounding waters. He also raised the possibility that noise from ships, bright artificial lights and electric fields generated by nearby facilities could be affecting the shark's senses. These explanations have not been confirmed, but they offer possible reasons for the animal's repeated return.Kim also told AP that the shark might need more time to adjust after spending so long in the canal. “The shark has been staying inside the canal for an extended period, so I didn’t expect it to head straight out into the open water,” he said. “It would be best to give it about a week to leave on its own,” he added.Bukangi has been identified as a female dusky shark, a species listed as endangered by the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN).Dusky sharks are found in tropical and temperate waters across the world. According to South Korea's National Institute of Fisheries Science, they can grow up to 4.2 metres long and travel considerable distances in search of suitable water conditions. They generally prefer temperatures between 18 and 26 degrees Celsius and feed on fish and squid. Their slow reproductive rate also makes the species vulnerable to population declines.Reuters also reported that experts have linked more frequent shark sightings along South Korea's east coast to warming ocean temperatures.
Article Summary: Female dusky shark, known locally as Bukangi, has been in the North Port canal in Busan, South Korea, since September 18. It was finally guided towards the open sea on Wednesday. But the rescue lasted only a few hours as the animal swam underneath a barrier net and returned to the canal.

Article Title: Old deeds and a 1926 condemnation judgment governed a 7.68-mile Florida rail corridor; when a public trail was proposed in 2019, landowners sought compensation, but a federal appeals court rejected th
Article Text:
Representative Image (AI-generated)

How the dispute began with a proposed trail

Why the old deeds became central to the case

What the 1926 condemnation judgment established

Why the appeals court rejected compensation

Old property deeds and a decades-old condemnation judgment have determined whether Florida landowners are entitled to compensation after a former railway corridor was considered for conversion into a public recreational trail. On October 22, 2026, the US Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit affirmed a lower court ruling that rejected claims involving approximately 7.68 miles of the Venice Branch railway corridor. According to the court’s opinion in Barron v. United States, published by Justia , the railway had acquired full ownership of the disputed land rather than merely an easement to operate trains on it. The ruling meant that the landowners had no reversionary property interests that were taken by the proposed trail arrangement, leaving them without grounds for compensation under the Fifth Amendment.The case arose after Seminole Gulf Railway, the corridor’s operator, filed a notice seeking an exemption to abandon the Venice Branch in March 2019. In response, the Sarasota County Board of County Commissioners asked the Surface Transportation Board (STB) to preserve the corridor for public use and interim trail development.The STB subsequently issued a Notice of Interim Trail Use (NITU) under the National Trails System Act Amendments of 1983.The mechanism allows an unused railway corridor to be preserved for potential recreational trail use instead of being legally abandoned, a process commonly known as railbanking.The arrangement can create a property dispute when a railway holds only an easement. Ordinarily, if railway operations end, the underlying property rights may revert to adjacent landowners under applicable state law. A NITU can prevent that reversion while the corridor remains available for trail use, potentially creating a compensable taking by the federal government.The landowners argued that this was precisely what had happened. They maintained that historical conveyance deeds and a 1926 condemnation judgment had granted the railroad only limited rights to use the land for railway purposes. They claimed the proposed trail arrangement interfered with their property interests and amounted to an unconstitutional taking without just compensation.The dispute depended on the distinction between an easement and ownership in fee simple. An easement generally grants a specific right to use another party’s property, while fee simple ownership represents a much broader ownership interest. The railway’s interest in the corridor originated partly in deeds from several former property owners and companies, including Sarasota Land Company, Clough, Burton, Neihardt, Florida Mortgage and Investment Company, and Ringling. The landowners argued that these transactions conveyed railway rights-of-way rather than complete ownership of the underlying land.However, the Federal Circuit agreed with the lower court that the deeds’ wording conveyed the land itself. The documents used broad language granting, selling and conveying the grantors’ rights, titles and interests in described parcels. Several also referred to the land being transferred forever, while one expressly stated that the conveyance was in fee simple. The court relied on Florida Supreme Court guidance that clear and unambiguous deed language must be applied as written. It rejected arguments that narrow strips of land, railway right-of-way terminology or the limited consideration stated in the deeds necessarily meant that only easements had been conveyed.A separate part of the dispute concerned a condemnation proceeding involving the Tampa Southern Railroad Company. The proceeding resulted in a jury award of $61,500 for property taken for railway use, followed by a judgment allowing the property to be appropriated as a railway right-of-way. Unlike the conveyance deeds, the condemnation judgment did not clearly establish whether the railroad acquired full ownership or only an easement. The Federal Circuit therefore examined additional records from the original proceeding, including proposed jury instructions submitted by both sides and a joint stipulation describing the property.Those documents showed that the parties and the jury had focused on the value of the land being taken, rather than simply the value of a right to use it. The court concluded that this evidence resolved the ambiguity in favour of fee simple ownership. The judges also rejected the landowners’ request to refer the legal question to the Florida Supreme Court, finding that existing Florida law provided sufficient guidance.The Federal Circuit affirmed the Court of Federal Claims’ decisions in the related cases, concluding that both the deeds and the condemnation judgment conveyed fee simple title to the railroad. Because the landowners had no remaining reversionary interests in the corridor, the STB’s notice did not take property interests belonging to them. The ruling did not establish that every railway right-of-way automatically grants full ownership. Instead, it turned on the wording of the specific historical documents and the additional evidence surrounding the 1926 condemnation proceeding.The decision highlights how property rights established generations ago can determine the outcome of modern disputes involving abandoned railway lines and public trails. In this case, the historical records proved decisive, and the landowners’ claims for compensation were rejected.
Article Summary: The US Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit affirmed a lower court ruling that rejected claims involving approximately 7.68 miles of the Venice Branch railway corridor. According to the court’s opinion in Barron v. United States, the railway had acquired full ownership of the disputed land rather than merely an easement. The ruling meant that the landowners had no reversionary property interests that were taken by the proposed trail arrangement.

Article Title: A developer bought a 0.59-acre Bel Air lot for $3.25 million in 2017 and spent nine years building a 10,950 sq ft brutalist mansion from 4,500 tons of reinforced concrete; it is now listed for $36.5 m
Article Text:
A mansion built around concrete

A nine-year development journey

Six bedrooms and luxury amenities

What the asking price means

A newly built mansion in Los Angeles' upscale Bel Air neighbourhood has hit the market for $36.5 million after a development journey spanning nearly nine years. The 10,946-square-foot residence, constructed using approximately 4,500 tons of reinforced concrete, occupies a 0.59-acre hillside lot and features cantilevered structures, expansive glass walls and an infinity pool. According to The Real Deal, which reported the listing on October 14, the property was developed by Tim McElwee and designed by architect Jeffrey Eyster.Located at 1331 Linda Flora Drive, the three-storey house was completed in 2026, according to its real estate listing. The Multiple Listing Service (MLS) records its area as 10,946 square feet, while the lot measures approximately 0.5854 acres. The asking price is $36.5 million, although the eventual sale price, if a transaction takes place, could differ.The residence stands out for its extensive use of reinforced concrete, a material more commonly associated with infrastructure and commercial buildings than luxury homes. Its design incorporates large cantilevered forms, angled columns and substantial overhangs that create the impression of heavy concrete volumes extending over the hillside.The architectural approach draws on brutalism, a style recognised for its emphasis on exposed materials, geometric forms and the visible expression of a building's structure.Rather than concealing the concrete behind conventional exterior finishes, the house makes the material central to its appearance.According to Mansion Global, which covered the property on October 12, approximately 4,500 tons of concrete went into the project. The property's listing describes the quantity as around 10 million pounds of reinforced concrete. Inside, board-formed concrete ceilings and polished terrazzo flooring are balanced by wood-panelled walls and expansive glass doors. The design connects the principal living spaces to outdoor terraces, making the surrounding hills and views part of the home's visual appeal.The project is associated with developer Tim McElwee and architect Jeffrey Eyster of Atelier Eyster Architecture. Hoodline, reporting on October 15, described the development as a nine-year journey that culminated in the newly completed mansion entering the market in 2026.Reports have placed McElwee's acquisition of the lot in 2017 at approximately $3.25 million. However, publicly displayed property records show a sale dated March 29, 2018, for $3.1 million. The difference in the reported purchase date and price has not been independently reconciled, so the precise acquisition details remain uncertain. The nine-year timeline should also be understood as the project's reported development journey, rather than proof that construction continued uninterrupted for the entire period. The listing identifies the property as newly built in 2026.The design makes use of the sloping site through multiple levels, terraces and projecting structural elements. Large glass surfaces contrast with the solidity of the concrete, creating a house that combines a heavy exterior with open views and light-filled interiors.Despite its industrial appearance, the mansion includes amenities associated with high-end Los Angeles real estate. The listing identifies six bedrooms and nine bathrooms, comprising eight full bathrooms and one half-bathroom. The primary suite occupies a dedicated level and opens onto a private roof garden. Its bathroom includes a terrazzo soaking tub. Other facilities include a screening room, gym, sauna, steam facilities and spa amenities.The kitchen features a large island and a separate preparation kitchen, while outdoor spaces include terraces and pools on different levels. These areas are designed to take advantage of the property's hillside setting and views across the surrounding landscape.The extensive use of concrete, sculptural architecture and private amenities distinguish the residence from more conventional luxury homes. Its design places equal emphasis on the material's mass and the views opened up by large expanses of glass.The $36.5 million figure is the seller's asking price, not a confirmed sale value. The property would need to attract a buyer willing to meet the asking price or negotiate an acceptable offer before its final market value could be established.The listing also comes amid scrutiny of high-value property transactions in Los Angeles. Hoodline noted the potential relevance of the city's Measure ULA transfer tax, which applies to qualifying real estate transactions. Any tax liability would depend on the final transaction value and the rules applicable at closing.For now, the mansion's listing highlights the scale of investment involved in creating architecturally distinctive homes in Bel Air, where privacy, views and individual design can be major selling points. Its unusual concrete construction and lengthy development history give the property a distinct identity in the luxury market, even as its eventual sale price remains uncertain.
Article Summary: The 10,946-square-foot residence occupies a 0.59-acre hillside lot and features cantilevered structures, expansive glass walls and an infinity pool. The three- storey house was completed in 2026, according to its real estate listing. It was developed by developer Tim McElwee and architect Jeffrey Eyster.

Article Title: Ohio lowered Guilford Lake by 20 feet for a $14 million dam rehabilitation project; the reservoir is expected to refill in 2027
Article Text:
PC: Ohio Department of Natural Resources

Why did Ohio lower Guilford Lake for dam rehabilitation

How will Ohio’s new spillway improve Guilford Lake Dam safety

What is the timeline for Guilford Lake’s $14 million project

Ohio has lowered Guilford Lake by 20 feet as part of a $14 million dam rehabilitation project to address structural deficiencies and meet modern safety requirements. According to the Ohio Department of Natural Resources (ODNR), the reservoir reached full drawdown during preparations for construction, which includes replacing the existing spillway and improving the dam’s drainage system and embankment stability. The work is intended to help the dam safely manage major flood events and protect downstream communities. Construction was reported to be on schedule in June 2026, with the lake expected to begin refilling in winter 2026–27 and reach normal levels by spring 2027, weather permitting.The rehabilitation follows engineering evaluations that identified deterioration in the dam’s concrete spillway, including separation at its joints. The existing spillway also lacked sufficient capacity to safely pass the Probable Maximum Flood (PMF), the largest flood considered in the project’s design requirements. ODNR said the dam’s embankment had insufficient safety factors for seepage and stability, while its internal drainage system had reached the end of its design life.The department stated that addressing these deficiencies was necessary to protect downstream communities and preserve Guilford Lake as a recreational resource.The dam has undergone several major interventions since its original construction, including a full reconstruction in 1933 and modifications in 1957, 1968 and 1983. The current rehabilitation is designed to bring the structure into compliance with modern dam safety regulations and prepare it for continued service in the coming decades.The rehabilitation includes a new labyrinth spillway designed to pass the Probable Maximum Flood without overtopping the dam’s embankment. According to ODNR, the design is intended to maintain the lake’s normal pool elevation once the reservoir returns to its usual operating level. It is also intended to keep downstream discharges during significant storm events consistent with pre-rehabilitation conditions.Work on the embankment involves excavating the existing structure to install a modern drainage and filter system with monitoring capabilities. The embankment will then be rebuilt and reinforced with additional material at its downstream toe. In its June 2026 update, ODNR reported that the existing spillway demolition had been completed and concrete had been poured for both the upper and lower cutoff walls of the new spillway. Installation of a new toe drain had also begun on the eastern side of the spillway, while the stilling basin at the base of the structure was the next component scheduled for concrete work.The Ruhlin Company was approved as the contractor after bids for the project were opened on 23 October 2025. ODNR reported that the project would cost approximately $14 million and that the state’s Controlling Board had approved the contractor and released the funding. Construction preparations included establishing a field office, installing perimeter fencing and signage, and putting erosion controls in place. A cofferdam made from sheet piling and water-control measures were also installed to allow the existing spillway to be demolished.Public access to the construction site remains prohibited, although the state park campground remains open. ODNR has stated that fishing is permitted outside the construction area, but swimming is prohibited throughout the lake. Vehicles are not allowed on the exposed lakebed, and the department has warned visitors to avoid ice because it may be unsafe as water levels change. The construction site is being monitored remotely, and periodic photographs of progress are available through the Guilford Lake State Park Facebook page.According to the project schedule published by ODNR, substantial completion of construction is anticipated in winter 2026–27, when the lake is expected to begin refilling. The department has identified spring 2027 as the target for completing the refill, subject to weather conditions. Although the lake will remain closed to the public during construction, ODNR does not anticipate long-term road closures, with most of the work expected to be accessed through the southeastern entrance. The rehabilitation is intended to address the dam’s identified safety deficiencies while restoring the reservoir to its normal operating level.
Article Summary: Ohio has lowered Guilford Lake by 20 feet as part of a $14 million dam rehabilitation project. The reservoir reached full drawdown during preparations for construction, which includes replacing the existing spillway and improving the dam’s drainage system and embankment stability. The work is intended to help the dam safely manage major flood events and protect downstream communities.

Article Title: Archaeologists uncovered a 15th-century ship beneath Barcelona during car park construction; its wooden hull had around 30 ribs
Article Text:
PC: Barcelona City Council

Medieval ship was discovered beneath Barcelona’s former fish market

PC: Barcelona City Council

How did archaeologists preserve Barcelona’s medieval ship

What did the ship reveal about 15th- and 16th-century shipbuilding

How did the car park project connect research and sustainable mobility

Archaeologists uncovered the remains of a medieval ship beneath Barcelona’s former fish market during construction work for a new car park. The vessel dated back to between the 15th and 16th centuries and offered further knowledge about the city’s maritime history. Provisionally named Ciutadella I, the discovered section measured around 10 metres in length and more than three metres in width.Its wooden structure included around 30 ribs and at least seven planks covering the hull. According to Barcelona City Council, the remains, which had been covered in sediment over time, were in a very fragile state of conservation as of 2025. Archaeologists began documenting and preserving the structure to protect it from further damage.The ship was found during construction work for a new car park on the site of the former Mercat del Peix. The section discovered, provisionally named Ciutadella I, measured 10 metres in length and more than three metres in width. Its structure consisted of around 30 wooden ribs, which formed the curved frame along the sides of the vessel, and at least seven strakes, or wooden planks covering the hull.The remains had been covered in sediment over time and were found in a very fragile state.The discovery provided further knowledge about the diversity and complexity of medieval maritime activity in Barcelona, including the sailing and naval construction techniques used in the city during the 15th and 16th centuries.The Barcelona Archaeology Service worked to document and conserve the ship after its discovery, advised by the Museu d’Arqueologia de Catalunya’s Underwater Archaeology Centre (CASC). The waterlogged wood was extremely sensitive, and drying could have caused it to fall apart. To prevent this, parts of the structure were covered with the original soil surrounding it.The initial conservation stage included three-dimensional documentation, labelling individual pieces, collecting samples, and preparing the remains for transfer into containers filled with water. The planned process also included desalination and the impregnation of the wood with water-soluble wax. The substance was intended to penetrate the material and strengthen its internal structure, helping ensure the remains could be preserved over the long term.The archaeological value of Ciutadella I lay in the information it provided about sailing and naval construction techniques used in Barcelona during the 15th and 16th centuries. The discovery added to evidence from another similar vessel found in 2008 near Estació de França. That ship was named Barceloneta I.The newly uncovered remains were being documented and conserved because of their fragile condition. Their wooden components and structure formed part of the archaeological evidence.The excavation was linked to the construction of a 7,000-square-metre car park designed as a sustainable mobility services hub. The facility was intended to serve the future Barcelona Biomedical Research complex of the Spanish National Research Council and Pompeu Fabra University.The development formed part of the Ciutadella del Coneixement strategy, a scientific and urban project intended to turn Parc de la Ciutadella and its surroundings into a leading European space for knowledge, dissemination, research and innovation. The excavation also generated 40,000 cubic metres of sand from Barcelona’s subsoil. This material was used to regenerate Sant Sebastià beach through a joint operation involving the Port of Barcelona and BSM.
Article Summary: Archaeologists uncovered the remains of a medieval ship beneath Barcelona’s former fish market during construction work for a new car park. The vessel dated back to between the 15th and 16th centuries. Its wooden structure included around 30 ribs and at least seven planks covering the hull. Archaeologists began documenting and preserving the structure to protect it from further damage.

Article Title: Kim Jong Un photos released to dismiss rumours of coma, takeover by sister
Article Text:
Kim Jong Un inspects pink shoe, women’s coats as death rumours grip North Korea

How the death rumours began

Claims of Chinese troop deployment

What is known about Kim's health?

North Korean supreme leader Kim Jong Un has resurfaced in photographs released by state media, inspecting children's footwear and women's clothing, after unverified claims circulated online that he had died from a brain haemorrhage.The photographs, published by North Korea's official media on Monday, show Kim examining footwear, gesturing towards officials and inspecting coats at a garment and footwear exhibition. The images emerged amid a wave of social media speculation about the 42-year-old leader's health and the possibility of a succession crisis in the secretive country, the New York Post reported.According to North Korea's official Korean Central News Agency, Kim toured the exhibition on Monday. However, the photographs have not been independently authenticated, and it remains unclear precisely when they were taken.One image shows Kim bending forward to inspect a small pink shoe held by a woman. In another, he gestures with his arms outstretched as he appears to address an official. A third photograph captures him reaching towards the sleeve of a woman's coat displayed on a mannequin.The speculation gathered pace after Wanjun Xie, a US-based Chinese dissident associated with the China Democracy Party, posted a series of claims on X alleging that Kim had died and that his sister, Kim Yo Jong , had taken control of the country.In a post on Monday, Xie wrote: "Rumours of the death of North Korean leader Kim Jong Un have been circulating online for days, but Kim Jong Un has not yet made a public appearance to deny them. This indirectly confirms that the rumours of Kim Jong Un's death are likely true. Furthermore, it is rumoured that after Kim Jong-un's death, the North Korean regime has not been transferred to his daughter Kim Ju-ae, but is currently in the hands of his sister Kim Yo-jong."After assuming power, Kim Yo-jong immediately activated loudspeaker broadcasts to South Korea and fired 201 warning shots. She also warned South Korea that North Korea was considering a comprehensive upgrade of its tactical strike capabilities. This sudden intensification of threats against South Korea is clearly aimed at strengthening her control over the North Korean military and consolidating her power through strong external threats. This indirectly confirms the rumors that Kim Jong-un is dead and that Kim Yo-jong is currently in control of the regime; these rumors are likely true."The New York Post reported that Xie's claims began gaining traction on Sunday. However, the allegations have not been supported by medical records, identifiable witnesses or other independently verifiable evidence.In another post on Sunday, Xie claimed that Kim had suffered a severe cerebral haemorrhage, fallen into a coma and been transferred to Beijing for emergency treatment. He alleged that a team of specialists from Peking Union Medical College Hospital had travelled to North Korea before Kim was moved to China."It is rumoured that recently, Kim Jong-un, General Secretary of the Workers' Party of Korea and Supreme Leader of North Korea, suffered a severe cerebral haemorrhage and fell into a coma. Although a team of medical experts from Peking Union Medical College Hospital was dispatched to North Korea to assist in his treatment, the poor medical conditions in North Korea forced Kim Jong-un to be transferred to Peking Union Medical College Hospital for emergency treatment. However, due to the severity of his condition and the fact that the optimal window for treatment had passed, Kim Jong-un succumbed to his injuries and died. His body has been secretly transported back to North Korea, and the news of his death is being kept under wraps."Xie further alleged that Kim's body had been secretly returned to North Korea and that authorities were concealing news of his death. He also claimed that Chinese troops had been deployed to Pyongyang amid fears of a succession crisis.In a separate post, he wrote: "It is said that on October 17, Peking Union Medical College Hospital dispatched a team of cardiovascular and cerebrovascular medical experts to North Korea to participate in the rescue of North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, who was in critical condition."Xie's posts also fuelled speculation about a possible power struggle involving Kim's daughter, Kim Ju-ae, and his sister, Kim Yo Jong. He claimed that China had sent 9,000 troops to Pyongyang to help stabilise the situation.The claims of Kim's death, a Chinese troop deployment and a possible succession crisis remain unverified. North Korean authorities have not explicitly addressed the death reports.Kim's health has long been the subject of international speculation. The New York Post reported that South Korea's National Intelligence Service told lawmakers on September 30 that Kim weighed approximately 140 kilograms (309 pounds) and faced an elevated risk of cardiovascular disease because of severe obesity.However, the agency reportedly detected no significant signs of ill health, pointing to Kim's ability to run up stairs during an inspection of a naval destroyer.The latest rumours echo a false alarm in 2020, when Ji Seong-ho, a North Korean defector who later became a South Korean lawmaker, claimed he was "99%" certain that Kim had died following cardiovascular surgery. Kim subsequently appeared in public, and Ji apologised for making the erroneous claim.The New York Post said it had sought comment from the governments of North Korea and China, as well as Peking Union Medical College Hospital.
Article Summary: North Korean supreme leader Kim Jong Un has resurfaced in photographs released by state media. The images emerged amid a wave of social media speculation about the 42-year-old leader's health and the possibility of a succession crisis. Unverified claims circulated online that he had died from a brain haemorrhage.

Article Title: Typhoon Champi: Taiwan issues land warning, cancels 125 flights as powerful storm approaches
Article Text:
Nasa's Terra satellite shows Typhoon Noul in the Pacific Ocean, approaching Taiwan and Japan's main islands on its northward journey (Reuters image)

Taiwan issued a land warning for powerful Typhoon Champi on Thursday and cancelled 125 flights as the storm approached the island's northeastern coast, bringing the threat of destructive winds, torrential rain and waves exceeding six metres, Reuters reported.Champi, which was previously classified as a super typhoon, weakened slightly but continued to pack gusts of more than 227 kmph near its centre, according to Taiwan's Central Weather Administration. The storm was about 520 km southeast of Taiwan's southern tip and was expected to pass close to the northeastern coast late on Friday before moving north towards the Chinese coast.Taiwan President Lai Ching-te urged residents to prepare for the storm and avoid mountainous and coastal areas."A little more preparation means less risk," he wrote on his Facebook page.Mobile phone alerts warning of waves exceeding six metres were issued to coastal towns, while rainfall approaching one metre was forecast in northern mountainous areas, including hills near the capital Taipei. Weather experts warned that the storm's impact could last nearly two days.Taiwan's transport ministry said 125 flights had been cancelled on Thursday, mostly domestic services, while the rail network remained unaffected.The interior ministry said no evacuations had been reported.Champi is also forecast to pass over Yonaguni, Japan's westernmost inhabited island in Okinawa Prefecture. Japan Airlines, ANA and Skymark cancelled more than 100 flights between Thursday and Sunday, mostly domestic services, disrupting travel for more than 11,000 passengers.
Article Summary: Taiwan issues land warning for powerful Typhoon Champi. 125 flights cancelled as storm approaches island's northeastern coast. Threat of destructive winds, torrential rain and waves exceeding six metres. Japan Airlines, ANA and Skymark cancel more than 100 flights between Thursday and Sunday.

Article Title: Explosion, fuel leak: Two Syrian pipelines damaged in fresh blow to war-hit energy network
Article Text:
Security forces of Syria's Interior Ministry guard the al-Omar oil field, the country's largest by area and production

Two pipelines carrying gas and petroleum products were damaged in separate incidents in Syria on Thursday, with one explosion triggering a fire and another causing a fuel leak, Syrian state media reported.According to the Syrian Arab News Agency (SANA), citing the state-owned Syrian Petroleum Company, an explosion struck the Jbessa gas pipeline in Hasakah province, while a separate leak was detected on the Baniyas-Homs petroleum-products pipeline near Homs.The explosion struck the Jbessa gas export pipeline in the al-Arabidi area of Hasakah province, setting the pipeline on fire. Emergency teams isolated the damaged section and shut valves to contain the blaze.The Syrian Petroleum Company described the incident as sabotage. Officials said alternative arrangements would maintain gas supplies to power stations during repairs, while domestic gas supplies remained unaffected.In a separate incident, a hole was discovered in the Baniyas-Homs pipeline in the Hadida area west of Homs, causing a leak of petroleum products. Emergency and technical teams were deployed to contain the leak and isolate the damaged section.Al Jazeera, citing Syrian state media, reported that the damage to the Baniyas-Homs pipeline was believed to be linked to an attempted fuel theft. The initial reports did not confirm the cause or identify those responsible.The incidents come amid a series of disruptions to Syria’s energy infrastructure. Earlier in October, an oil pipeline near Tal Hamis in Hasakah province was damaged in what the Syrian Petroleum Company described as sabotage.Syria is working to rebuild its oil and gas infrastructure after years of conflict, restoring production in northeastern oilfields and reconnecting them with processing facilities and refineries in Homs and Baniyas.In January 2026, the Syrian Petroleum Company began pumping raw gas from the Jbessa fields in Hasakah to the Furqlus gas plant in Homs countryside at around 1.2 million cubic metres per day to support electricity generation.The second damaged pipeline, connecting Baniyas on the Mediterranean coast to Homs, transports petroleum products between two important energy centres. The Baniyas refinery is undergoing an overhaul aimed at increasing its processing capacity from around 80,000 to 130,000 barrels per day.Syria has also undertaken emergency pipeline repairs and plans to expand its transportation network. A September 2026 analysis by the Baker Institute for Public Policy reported that the Syrian Petroleum Company was repairing existing infrastructure and planning a heavy-crude pipeline linking northeastern oilfields to the Baniyas refinery.
Article Summary: Two pipelines carrying gas and petroleum products were damaged in separate incidents in Syria on Thursday. One explosion struck the Jbessa gas export pipeline in the al-Arabidi area of Hasakah province, setting the pipeline on fire. Emergency teams isolated the damaged section and shut valves to contain the blaze. A separate leak was detected on the Baniyas-Homs petroleum-products pipeline near Homs.

Article Title: Kylie Jenner launched a lip kit in 2015 and built a global cosmetics brand; Coty agreed to pay $600 million for a 51% stake in 2019
Article Text:
Image: Left/Britannica/Right/Refinery29

How the November 2015 Kylie Lip Kit launch became Kylie Cosmetics, a beauty brand with global reach

Kylie Cosmetics stand at Melbourne Airport, Australia. Image Credit: Wikipedia

Why Coty agreed to pay 600 million dollars for 51 per cent ownership of the Kylie Jenner partnership

Kylie Jenner arrives at the Vanity Fair Oscar Party on Sunday, March 15, 2026, at the Los Angeles County Museum of Art in LA.

177 million dollars in revenue, growth targets and the financial case for Coty

How creative control, licensing and Coty's manufacturing reach shaped the global beauty expansion plan

Where Coty stands today as a global beauty company and how the Kylie Jenner partnership fits its plans

Few beauty stories capture the power of social media as clearly as the rise of Kylie Jenner 's cosmetics business. What began in November 2015 as a debut lip kit became Kylie Cosmetics, a brand that built a devoted audience online and then attracted one of the largest beauty companies in the world. In November 2019, that company, Coty, agreed to buy a majority stake in the business for 600 million dollars. Here’s how the brand grew, what the agreement contained, why the numbers mattered, and how the partnership was designed to carry the business into new global markets. The deal also marked a turning point in the influencer-led beauty industry, demonstrating how a strong digital following could translate into a valuable global consumer brand.Coty's press release describes the origin story plainly. In November 2015, Kylie Jenner launched Kylie Cosmetics, and the debut product, the Kylie Lip Kit, was a sell-out success. Her online store, KylieCosmetics.com, is one of the most successful online stores in the world, and the range grew well beyond lips to include eyeliners, eyeshadows, blushes, highlighters, concealers, brushes and makeup bags, plus limited edition sets released throughout the year.In May 2019, she introduced Kylie Skin, a range of skincare products. The audience behind it was enormous, Coty says she has more than 270 million followers across her personal and brand social media channels, and that both brands are among the fastest-growing and most-engaged beauty brands on social media. Forbes featured her as the youngest-ever self-made billionaire in August 2018.On 18 November 2019, Coty and Kylie Jenner announced a long-term strategic partnership. Under the terms of the agreement, Coty would acquire 51 per cent ownership in the partnership for 600 million dollars, and the acquisition was expected to close in the third quarter of Coty's fiscal year 2020. Coty described the transaction as a key milestone in its ongoing transformation into a more focused and agile company. Chairman of the Board Peter Harf told the public that the partnership was an exciting step in Coty's renewed emphasis on its beauty business, calling Kylie Jenner a modern-day icon with an incredible sense of the beauty consumer. Pierre Laubies, Coty's chief executive officer, told the public the company was pleased to welcome her into its organisation and family.Coty's press release sets out the financial case in specific terms. Kylie Cosmetics generated an estimated 177 million dollars in net revenues over the preceding twelve months. Coty said it expected the transaction to add more than 1 per cent per year to the net revenue growth of its core fragrance, cosmetics and skin care portfolio over the next three years. The company also expected the deal to be neutral to its earnings per share in the first year and to add to them afterwards, and it expected the return on invested capital to exceed its cost of capital by fiscal year 2023. Tiger Shark served as an advisor to Coty on the transaction. Coty also scheduled a conference call that morning, with the live audio webcast and presentation slides made available through its investor relations website.The agreement divides responsibilities along each side's strengths. Together, Coty and Kylie Jenner set and lead the strategic direction, focusing on global expansion and entry into new beauty categories. Kylie Jenner and her team keep leading all creative efforts in product and communications, building on her global reach through social media. Coty takes overall responsibility for developing the portfolio, drawing on its knowledge of research and development, manufacturing, distribution and commercial strategy, and it acts as licensee for skincare, fragrances and nail products. All beauty categories continue to be sold through leading luxury beauty retailers and owned digital channels. Both parties aim to build what Coty calls a high-growth, digitally native beauty brand. Kylie Jenner told the public the partnership lets her team stay focused on creating and developing each product while building an international beauty powerhouse.Coty's own investor relations website shows the scale of the company that Kylie Jenner partnered with. Founded in Paris in 1904, Coty describes itself as one of the world's largest beauty companies, with a portfolio spanning fragrance, colour cosmetics, and skin and body care. The site lists the company as second globally in both fragrances and mass colour cosmetics, with more than 60 brands and licenses, about 11,300 employees, seven manufacturing sites and sales in more than 120 countries. For fiscal 2026, it reports net revenues of 5.8 billion dollars, adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation of 847 million dollars, and free cash flow of 348 million dollars. Pairing that infrastructure with a creator-led brand is what the partnership set out to do.
Article Summary: Coty and Kylie Jenner announced a long-term strategic partnership. Under the terms of the agreement, Coty would acquire 51 per cent ownership in the partnership for 600 million dollars. The acquisition was expected to close in the third quarter of Coty's fiscal year 2020. Both parties aim to build what Coty calls a high-growth beauty brand.

Article Title: 7.0-magnitude earthquake hits China’s Tibet, atleast 16 killed, 46 injured- watch
Article Text:
People run outside of buildings as earthquake strike China

At least 16 people were killed and 46 others injured after a powerful 7.0-magnitude earthquake struck Baqen County in Nagqu City, in China’s Xizang region, at 10:33 pm on Thursday.According to the United States Geological Survey (USGS), the earthquake occured with its epicentre about 191 kilometres east-north-east of Nagqu. The area is sparsely populated and lies at a high altitude in northern Tibet. The USGS estimated the quake's depth at 18 kilometres below the Earth's surface.Nagqu lies more than 300 kilometres north of Lhasa, the capital of Tibet.Authorities have begun relief operations in the affected area, with emergency supplies reaching the quake-hit zone early Friday.China Xinhua News released a series of images on X showing the devastation caused by the earthquake.In X post, it wrote, "Relief materials allocated by authorities at various levels include 1,000 sets of prefabricated houses, more than 3,200 tents and over 2,800 folding beds. Essential supplies such as quilts, stoves and clothing are also being sent to support people affected by the earthquake."
Article Summary: Powerful 7.0-magnitude earthquake struck Baqen County in Nagqu City, in China’s Xizang region, at 10:33 pm on Thursday. The area is sparsely populated and lies at a high altitude in northern Tibet.
